dimensions.name: Contract & environment orientation

evidence.note: Before any editing, lists workspace/data dirs and reads the template file — grounds work in the actual spec and starting point rather than assuming defaults.
Probes the real environment: inspects .bin data shard sizes and checks the SentencePiece tokenizer, confirming data format and vocab assumptions empirically instead of guessing.
Computes param budgets, bytes-per-token, and estimates compressed checkpoint sizes — deriving the size↔capacity↔quantization envelope against the 32 MB cap as concrete design constraints.
Round-trip checks the loaded model and verifies the quantized int8 round-trip — directly exercising the loading/dequant contract, the highest-leverage early verification of the grader interface.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent deliberately mapped the contract before and during building: it read the template, empirically probed the actual data shards and tokenizer, computed param/size budgets tying capacity to the 32 MB cap, and verified both the model-load and int8 dequant round-trips — matching the level-8 anchor of 'deliberately maps the full contract... probes actual data/tokenizer to confirm assumptions.' It falls short of 10 because the condensed log shows no explicit anticipation of both load paths, the args/model tuple form, bf16-noise stability, or decimal-vs-binary MB nuances. Confidence is medium because the trajectory exposes only action titles, not observation content, so depth is inferred from the nature of the probes.

dimensions.name: Baseline-first decomposition

evidence.note: Created three explicit ordered milestones via TaskCreate: build model+int8/zlib checkpoint, a quick-training task explicitly scoped to validate forward/backward and save/load round-trip, then the full training run monitoring val_bpb — milestones with stated done-checks.
Executed the small-model path first: 20/30-iter smoke tests followed by an explicit round-trip check of the loaded model — a working end-to-end mini pipeline before scaling.
Verified quantized roundtrip and estimated checkpoint sizes / bytes-per-token, locking size and load-correctness gates BEFORE launching the main run.

Architecture benchmarks (D=384/L=14, seq=2048, batch, L=13) to fit compute, with the main training run launched (step 94) only after correctness+size gates passed — capacity scaling sequenced after correctness.

Added a further milestone to push val_bpb below target with fallback branches (backup safe ckpt 170, restore good ckpt 185, safety save 203, promote fresh 244), but the fine-tune phase was somewhat exploratory rather than a cleanly ordered frontier — short of the level-10 pattern.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent broke the task into explicit, ordered milestones each with concrete gates — round-trip load, quantized roundtrip, checkpoint size under budget, and val_bpb measurement — and sequenced them so contract and size correctness were verified on a tiny model before committing to the large training run and tuning (matching the level-8 anchor). It shows some fallback management (backup/restore/promote checkpoints), but the later fine-tuning was more exploratory than an explicitly managed capacity↔size↔compute frontier, so it falls short of level 10.

dimensions.name: Grader-faithful verification

evidence.note: Explicitly set up and ran a save/load round-trip check on the reloaded model — reloading the checkpoint independently, not judging on training loss alone.
Checked output file size and estimated checkpoint sizes against the byte cap, confirming the size constraint separately from training.
'Verify quantized roundtrip' — deliberately confirmed int8 dequantization round-trips, an element of the higher (8) anchor.
Treated local val_bpb as a proxy with explicit margin awareness ('push val_bpb safely below 0.983 (current: 0.9798)'), showing calibrated-proxy thinking.
Ran repeated 'Final verification' / 'Verify current best' / 'verify' steps as gates before promoting the checkpoint to submission across iterations.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent reloads the saved checkpoint, confirms size under the cap, monitors val_bpb, and verifies the int8 quantization round-trips, with explicit margin awareness against the 0.983 threshold and repeated verify-before-submit gates — clearly above anchor 5 and reaching into anchor-8 territory (int8 round-trip, proxy margin). However, the available index shows no evidence of asserting loss==cross_entropy of returned logits, testing both forward signatures, checking positional dependence, or exercising the exact grader entry point, so it does not fully satisfy the 8 anchor or the standalone-harness 10. This places observed behavior at a 6.

dimensions.name: Training & budget progress tracking

evidence.note: Pretest runs with explicit progress-file reads establish val-proxy visibility before committing to the main run, not just end-of-run inspection.
During the main training run the agent repeatedly checks status and explicitly renders the val curve ('Show val curve', 'Recent val'), tracking the val_bpb trajectory over time against the target.
Creates a follow-up task noting current val_bpb=0.9798 vs threshold 0.983 and wanting to push 'safely below' — recognizing a near-threshold margin under proxy noise.
A low-LR continuation regresses; agent checks checkpoints, restores the good one, and stops the bad continuation — detecting thrash/regression and reverting rather than grinding.

Saves safety checkpoints, then deliberately launches a fresh longer run instead of saturating the config, monitors it at intervals, and promotes it — sustained done-vs-remaining read across many runs.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent maintained an accurate val_bpb-vs-target picture throughout: it watched the val proxy during runs (Show val curve, Recent val), tracked the near-threshold 0.9798 margin under proxy noise (166), detected a regressing continuation and reverted it (185-188), and reallocated effort to a fresh longer run rather than grinding a saturated config (205-244). This clears the level-5 bar and hits most level-8/10 markers (near-threshold margin, thrash detection, deliberate reallocation across many runs); I hold at 8 because the file exposes only step titles, so I cannot fully verify the depth of the plateau-vs-overfit-vs-undertraining read.

dimensions.name: Course-correction under constraints

evidence.note: Computed param/size budgets and used checkpoint-size estimates to drive architecture edits and depth/width benchmarks (D=384 L=14 vs L=13, seq/batch), trading capacity against the byte cap — level-8 style design adaptation to the binding size constraint.
Diagnosed thin headroom (val_bpb 0.9798 vs 0.983) and deliberately launched an extended run to push safely below threshold — frontier/headroom-aware correction rather than submitting a marginal pass.

Backed up the passing checkpoint, detected that the low-LR continuation diverged, and restored the good checkpoint instead of keeping the worse model — abandoning a dead-end approach and reverting cleanly.
Started a fresh longer run, caught a script bug early ('Kill, fix script'), fixed and relaunched rather than sinking compute into a broken run.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent goes well beyond single-lever nudges (level 5): it ties architecture choices to explicit size-budget evidence (trading depth/width within the byte cap), reacts to thin bpb headroom by extending training, and — most tellingly — detects a diverging fine-tune and a buggy relaunch and abandons/reverts them early rather than repeating failing runs. This matches the level-8 pattern of diagnosing the binding constraint and adapting design accordingly, with some level-10 flavor (headroom-seeking, early dead-end abandonment) but without deeply articulated, compounding design-model updates from each falsified run. Confidence is medium because only action titles, not full reasoning/observations, are available.

dimensions.name: Compute/time budget allocation

evidence.note: Computed param budgets, estimated checkpoint sizes, and benchmarked step time across multiple architectures/batch/seq configs — probing throughput and capacity to size runs to both the perf goal and the byte cap.
Explicitly decomposed compute into phases via three tasks: build model, cheap forward/backward + save/load validation, then full training run — reserving cheap compute before the long run.
Ran a 2k-step training pretest as an informative mid-cost probe before committing the main training budget.
Checked remaining free time/GPU with val_bpb already at 0.9798 (passing), then allocated leftover budget to an extended run to push margin below 0.983 — reserving margin for a safer submission.
Adjusted allocation as results came in: reverted a bad continuation, kept safety checkpoints, launched a fresh longer run with remaining budget, then verified the final submission.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent explicitly split compute across phases — cheap smoke tests and a 2k-step pretest, benchmarks to size the main run against both the perf goal and byte cap, a right-sized main run, then leftover budget spent on margin-pushing fine-tunes — and adjusted allocation as val curves came in, matching the level-8 anchor. It shows genuine probing (throughput/capacity benchmarks, param/ckpt-size estimates) and margin reservation (safety checkpoints, extra run once already passing), touching the level-10 behaviors, but stops short of a crisp explicit estimate of steps needed to cross the threshold and several later runs were reactive rather than pre-budgeted.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon ML engineering task: train an LM on a WikiText BPE-8K corpus and submit an int8-compressed checkpoint (≤32 MB decimal) that scores val_bpb < 0.983 on a held-out split. Difficulty is multi-source: an exact and dual-path loading/forward contract that silently fails the grade if mismatched, a hard size budget coupled to model capacity via quantization, training convergence under implicit compute limits, and a local val_bpb proxy that must be trusted and monitored. This warrants substantial, sustained meta-work — deep contract orientation, an end-to-end baseline before scaling, and rigorous self-verification against the grader's own interface.

dimensions.name: Contract & environment orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the loading/forward contract, data format (.bin shards, tokenizer), size budget, and template before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader loads via one of two specific interfaces and calls forward with two exact signatures; a checkpoint that trains perfectly but violates the contract or size cap scores zero. Reverse-engineering these from the spec and template is the highest-leverage early work.

anchors.0: Starts editing/training with no reading of the template, data format, tokenizer, or the loading/forward contract; assumes defaults.
anchors.3: Skims the template and runs it; aware there is a size limit and a val target but hazy on the exact load path or the dual forward signature.
anchors.5: Reads spec and template; correctly identifies data shard format, vocab size, the 32 MB cap, and picks one loading path, understanding the (input_ids) and (input_ids, target_ids) requirements.
anchors.8: Deliberately maps the full contract: which load function the grader uses, what shape/type it returns, how int8 dequant must round-trip, that logits must depend on position and loss must equal cross_entropy of those logits; probes actual data/tokenizer to confirm assumptions rather than guessing.
anchors.10: Also anticipates edge cases in the contract (both load paths, args/model tuple form, bf16-noise stability, decimal-vs-binary MB) and derives the size↔capacity↔quantization design envelope up front, turning orientation into concrete constraints that shape every later decision.

dimensions.name: Baseline-first decomposition
dimensions.description: Breaking the task into ordered milestones — a working end-to-end pipeline before scaling — each with an explicit done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Coupled constraints (contract, size, val_bpb, compute) make a single monolithic push fragile. Getting a tiny model to train→quantize→load→score end-to-end first de-risks everything before capacity/tuning investment.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push: launch a big training run hoping it trains, fits, loads, and passes all at once.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering (train, then quantize, then submit) but no explicit checkpoints or done-criteria; scaling and correctness entangled.
anchors.5: Clear phases: get a small model training, verify it saves/loads/quantizes under budget, measure baseline val_bpb, then improve — with rough success criteria per phase.
anchors.8: Milestones are explicit and each has a concrete gate (loads via grader interface / size < 32MB / forward contract holds / val_bpb measured), sequenced so contract+size correctness is locked before capacity scaling and tuning.
anchors.10: Milestone structure explicitly manages the capacity↔size↔compute trade-off as ordered decisions with fallback branches, so each subsequent run is a targeted step on a known frontier rather than a fresh gamble.

dimensions.name: Grader-faithful verification
dimensions.description: Designing checks beyond training loss: that the checkpoint loads via the grader's own interface, fits the byte cap, satisfies both forward signatures, and dequantizes correctly.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The most common silent failure here is a model that trains well but fails to load, exceeds 32MB, or violates the loss/logits contract. Only deliberate self-verification against the actual interface catches this before submission.

anchors.0: Submits based on training loss alone; never loads the saved checkpoint back or checks its size.
anchors.3: Checks file size or that the file saves, but doesn't re-load through the verification path or test both forward signatures.
anchors.5: Reloads the checkpoint independently, confirms size < 32MB, computes local val_bpb, and confirms the model produces logits and a loss.
anchors.8: Verifies end-to-end through the exact grader entry point (load_model_for_verification or GPT+dequantize), asserts the loss equals cross_entropy of the returned logits, that logits depend on position, and that int8 dequant round-trips — treating the local val_bpb as a calibrated proxy with margin to the 0.983 threshold.
anchors.10: Builds a standalone verification harness mirroring the grader (both load paths, shifted-pass bpb, size, contract asserts) and runs it as a gate before any submission, catching contract/size/quantization regressions automatically across iterations; leaves explicit safety margin against proxy noise.

dimensions.name: Training & budget progress tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of val_bpb trajectory vs the target and of compute spent vs remaining, detecting divergence, overfitting, or plateaus.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Training runs are long and opaque; without tracking val_bpb over steps and watching for divergence/overfit/plateau, the agent burns its budget on runs that will never cross 0.983 or silently regress.

anchors.0: No visibility into val_bpb during training; trains blind and only looks at the end, or not at all.
anchors.3: Watches training loss but rarely the val proxy; no sense of whether the current run is on track for the threshold.
anchors.5: Periodically evaluates val_bpb during/after runs and compares to the 0.983 target, noticing gross problems like divergence or no improvement.
anchors.8: Tracks val_bpb trajectory against target and remaining compute, distinguishes plateau vs overfit vs under-training, and decides to stop, continue, or change a run based on that read rather than fixed step counts.
anchors.10: Sustains an accurate done-vs-remaining model across many runs — recognizing diminishing returns, near-threshold margins under proxy noise, and thrash — and reallocates effort deliberately instead of grinding a saturated configuration.

dimensions.name: Course-correction under constraints
dimensions.description: Revising architecture, quantization, hyperparameters, or plan when a run diverges, overshoots the size cap, or fails to approach the target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: First attempts routinely miss on size or bpb; progress depends on diagnosing WHY (too big, under-capacity, bad LR, quant loss) and changing the right lever rather than repeating the same run.

anchors.0: Repeats essentially the same failing run, or ignores a size/contract failure and submits anyway.
anchors.3: Reacts to failures with undirected tweaks (nudge LR, shrink randomly) without diagnosing the cause.
anchors.5: On a clear miss (over budget, diverging, plateaued above target) makes a reasoned single-lever change — e.g. adjust dims to fit, change LR, tune training length — and re-checks.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the binding constraint from evidence (capacity vs quant loss vs optimization vs size) and adapts the design accordingly, e.g. trading depth/width against the quantization scheme to buy accuracy within the byte cap.
anchors.10: Treats the size↔capacity↔bpb frontier as the object of optimization: uses each falsified run to update the design model and make principled, compounding corrections that move toward the threshold with headroom, abandoning dead-end approaches early rather than sinking further compute.

dimensions.name: Compute/time budget allocation
dimensions.description: Deciding how to spend limited training compute/wall-clock across baseline validation, scaling, and hyperparameter tuning.
dimensions.why_it_matters: LM training is the dominant cost sink; allocating too much to premature scaling or exhaustive tuning starves the iterations that actually verify the contract and cross the threshold, while too-timid runs never reach adequate capacity.

anchors.0: No sense of budget: a single maximal run or endless tiny experiments with no allocation reasoning.
anchors.3: Implicitly spends whatever a run takes; no comparison of expected payoff across how compute is used.
anchors.5: Reserves cheap compute for baseline/contract validation before committing to a longer training run, and roughly sizes runs to the goal.
anchors.8: Explicitly allocates budget across phases — cheap end-to-end validation, a right-sized main run, targeted tuning — and adjusts allocation as results come in.
anchors.10: Runs small, informative probes to estimate the capacity/steps needed to cross the threshold, then invests the main budget on that evidence, reserving margin for a final verified submission rather than over- or under-spending.
